digest.text: Much of the air traffic across the U.S. was suddenly shut down Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for all departing flights “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.”
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration grounded all departing flights nationwide after a communications failure hit air traffic control centers.
All flights in the United States were grounded late Friday afternoon by the Federal Aviation Administration, just the second time since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
Sources told CBS News an update to the network connecting the air traffic control system caused a reboot, crash and outage.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. flights, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed Friday.
